comments.author: Poornachandra Kongara
comments.comment: Evals are the component I see overlooked most often. An agent can pass 20 happy-path prompts and still fail on tool timeouts, partial results, or adversarial inputs. Start with a small regression set before scaling agents. Which failure mode surprised you first? #AgentOps

comments.author: Carlos Budiman
comments.comment: For offsec agents, I’d rank models by eval pass-rate per dollar on a fixed harness, not vibes. A model that needs 20 retries to dodge guardrails can burn more than a stricter model that solves once. Are you tracking refusal rate, task completion, and token cost separately? #AgenticAI

comments.author: Shivani Virdi
comments.comment:
The refine count is the best production signal here. It separates retrieval misses from reasoning misses without guessing. Did you bucket refine count by course module?

#AgenticAI #Evals #RAG

comments.author: AI For Executives
comments.comment:
Most AI projects don't fail because the model is weak.
They fail because evaluation comes too late.
I've seen agents pass a demo and break on real tool calls.
What eval metric do you use before production?

#AIEvaluation #AgenticAI #LLMs

comments.author: Mervin Praison ✅
comments.comment: I keep seeing this pattern: the harness can move a model from 30% to 100% without changing weights. That makes step-level traces and evals the first budget line, not a later cleanup task. Which harness layer gives you the most pain right now: routing, state, tools, or guardrails? #AgenticAI #LLMEvals

comments.author: Manoj Ganapathi
comments.comment: Agents amplify the bottleneck, not remove it. When requirements, tests, and release ownership are split, more agent throughput just creates more inventory and more review debt. I would start by measuring one thing: time from accepted story to production signal, not PR count or token burn. What is the smallest end-to-end slice you can put agents behind: one story, one test suite, one deployable service?

comments.author: Jason Low 刘子杰
comments.comment: I’d shift the eval boundary from model output to harness side effects: file writes, shell commands, tool calls, and permission denials. ACP can standardize sessions, but capability parity is where orchestration gets fragile. How do you score non-deterministic harnesses when one has subagents and another does not? #AgenticAI #Evals
